source.title: A Gram-Gauss-Newton Method Learning Overparameterized Deep Neural Networks for Regression Problems
source.authors: Tianle Cai; Rui-Qi Gao; Jikai Hou; Siyu Chen; Dong Wang; Di He; Zhi-Hua Zhang; Li-Wei Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study reports training results for ResNetFixup on regression tasks, extending the Fixup claim to a different task setting. It does not test the CIFAR classification, depth, initialization-speed, or learning-rate claims.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports theoretical convergence results for GGN on overparameterized networks, but those are regression theory, not results on the claim versions. Cited findings from other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses Fixup and residual architectures to evaluate its GGN optimizer on regression tasks. It reports optimizer performance, without testing depth degradation, shortcut effects, initialization effects, or training speed and stability attributable to normalization. Successful GGN training of ResNetFixup alone does not test V3 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that GGN compares favorably with SGD on two regression tasks using standard architectures. More precisely, they prove quadratic convergence for full-batch GGN and linear convergence for mini-batch GGN under their assumptions; experiments show faster training and better reported RSNA test performance.
record.recipe_differences: The claim concerns shortcut effects on classification training; this paper studies regression with GGN and SGD, and uses ResNet-32 with Fixup or batch normalization. It does not isolate the shortcut effect.
record.method_sensitivity: On AFAD-LITE, GGN with ResNetFixup reaches nearly zero training loss in 30 epochs, while both SGD baselines decay more slowly.

fits_no_version.finding: On AFAD-LITE, GGN+ResNetFixup reaches nearly zero training loss within 30 epochs and converges faster than both SGD baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GGN can accelerate squared-loss regression training of ResNet-32 relative to the tested momentum-SGD recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Under explicit width, smoothness, initialization, and Gram-matrix assumptions, full-batch GGN has quadratic convergence and cyclic mini-batch GGN has linear convergence to zero regression loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide two-layer networks admit provable convergence under GGN for squared-loss regression.

record.problems: The reported experiments are regression tasks rather than classification; only GGN is tested on ResNetFixup, so the optimizer and normalization comparisons are not matched. Curves provide no stated numerical uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: None. The paper also shows RSNA Bone Age curves and reports faster convergence for GGN, but that task uses warm-start initialization from the first task; it does not add a distinct result on Fixup trainability from random initialization.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels, under SGD or Adam and variations in size, training duration, and regularization.
Spurious minima in ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, plain versus residual networks, special initialization of deep plain networks, and a comparative test of residual training without normalization.
Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth, signal and gradient propagation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Training above the initial stability limit, transient loss growth, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Speed and learning-rate tolerance attributable to batch normalization, and whether Fixup matches normalized residual networks in training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V3 verdicts. Comparing SGD against GGN does not limit the scope of a claim about depth, shortcuts, or normalization. Section 4.1 does include both normalization variants under SGD, contrary to the record's assertion, but the supplied figure text provides no readable comparison establishing their relative speed or stability.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam from random initialization, and model size or training-duration effects.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus shortcut depth comparisons; classification tasks; whether plain batch-normalized networks stall; the same optimizer and initialization compared with and without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, depth sweeps, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initializations.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness measurements, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance attributable to batch normalization in the stated classification settings.

rows.subject: ResNetFixup
rows.operation_detail: GGN training with Fixup initialization on AFAD-LITE regression data
rows.note: The text reports this outcome for GGN; the paper describes the model as ResNet-32 with Fixup initialization.
rows.check: The nearly zero loss by 30 epochs is correctly reported, but measures the study's own optimizer performance. It establishes neither the depth/shortcut comparison in V3 nor the speed and stability comparison in V6. Thirty epochs is a convergence milestone, not a stated total training duration.

rows.subject: ResNetFixup
rows.operation_detail: SGD with momentum on AFAD-LITE regression data
rows.note: The text states that this SGD baseline decays much slower than GGN in wall-clock time and epochs; the precise value is only shown in the figure.
rows.check: This is an optimizer comparator, not evidence of partial depth degradation or partial Fixup effectiveness. Slower convergence than GGN does not qualify V3 or V6. The supplied figure text does not resolve its speed relative to SGD+ResNetBN.

rows.subject: ResNetBN
rows.operation_detail: SGD with momentum on AFAD-LITE regression data
rows.note: The text states that this SGD baseline decays much slower than GGN in wall-clock time and epochs; the precise value is only shown in the figure.
rows.check: This is an optimizer comparator. Slower convergence than GGN+ResNetFixup confounds optimizer and normalization and cannot establish a normalization effect. Its comparison with SGD+ResNetFixup is not quantified or described in the supplied text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNetFixup trained with GGN on AFAD-LITE regression
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that training loss quickly becomes nearly zero in 30 epochs (R1). This supports the Fixup trainability component in this regression setting.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported SGD training curves decay much more slowly than GGN, and the study does not compare the two normalization settings under the same optimizer (R2, R3).
